text:
Someone wants to know what time it is in another city.
what time is it in Tokyo
time in lagos now
what tiem is it in cairo
Can you point me to the time in Sydney? I want to call before my bath.
It's every Sunday that I call my sister in Lima, so what time is it there now?
Is it too late to phone Berlin?
Could you please tell me the local time in Mumbai, because I do not want to wake anyone up?

A restaurant lets you book a table by choosing a day, a time and how many people are coming. If plans change, you can move the booking to a later time or ask for six seats instead of four. The menu shows the price of every dish, and many places also have a takeaway menu. Opening hours change with the seasons, and on days when it starts to snow, some places close early. People often ask, are you open tonight? A gentle way to change a booking is to say, could we come at eight o'clock instead? A short, clear request works best: the day, the time and the number of people.

Someone wants directions to the train station without using the motorway.
route to the station, no motorway
How do I get to the station? Not the motorway please.
Sorry, but can you find a way to the station with no toll roads?
Directions to the station, I don't want the highway.
The snow is starting to melt and the main road floods, so please don't send me that way.
I have a problem with heights, so no bridges, just get me to the station.
Could you show me a drive to the station that doesn't go through the city centre?

Lukas pulled over, unplugged the phone from the charger and looked at the clock. The tank was full, but a flat parcel was waiting at the post office, and Lukas did not know if it was open. "Hey phone, is the post office on Mill Street open now?" The assistant said it was open until five. Lukas thought for a moment. "Good. Remind me to check the mailbox every Monday at nine, and tell me when a parcel comes." The assistant said it had made a reminder for every Monday at nine, called check the mailbox. Lukas said thank you, plugged the phone back in and drove to Mill Street.

Bo is a grandparent who plans the school lunches for two grandchildren. On Sunday, Bo said to the kitchen speaker, "Please plan this week's lunches and make a shopping list from them." The speaker gave five easy lunches, one for each school day, and put everything needed on a list. Bo wanted to hear it clear and slow, so the speaker read it out. It had bread, cheese, apples and a dozen eggs. Then Bo remembered something. "One of the children cannot eat nuts. Reset the plan and leave out the peanut butter." The speaker reset the week with no nuts at all, put egg salad on Tuesday instead, and told Bo the list had changed. Bo nodded and went to find a coat for the shops.

Many people take medicine at set times, and a reminder helps them not to forget a dose. A dose is the amount you take each time, such as one pill with water. Doctors say how long to continue, and some medicines work best if you drink a full glass of water with them. People say, remind me to take my pill at eight every morning, or move my reminder to nine. They also change doctor's appointments. They say, book me in for next Friday, or make it the final slot of the day. Many people put a star next to the visits they must not miss. Simple words and a clear time are enough.

Someone wants to know how many days are left until a date.
how many days till friday
days until my birthday?
how mny days to christmas
How long until the big match on the ninth? I want to cheer for my team.
I have a bike wheel to pick up on the twentieth, so how many days is that from today?
The party is on the fourteenth at six sharp, so how many days do I still have?
Could you please tell me how many sleeps are left until the holiday?

Someone wants the phone to start recording a video.
start recording
record a video
start the camra
Is the camera working? Please film this.
My dad is about to laugh at his birthday cake, so start a video now.
Can you start a video? The radio is playing our song and I want to keep it.
I would like to film the dog in the garden, could you begin recording, please?

A huge storm hit the town, and the lights went out at Keisha's house. Keisha, a retired teacher, sat in the dark with a cold cup of tea and spoke to the phone. "The power is off and there is ice on the road outside. How long will it be out?" The assistant looked up the power company and said the repairs would take about two hours, maybe more if the ice got thicker. "Then I need more light," said Keisha. The assistant turned on the phone's torch at half brightness to save the battery, and said it would continue to check the power company every ten minutes. Keisha lit two candles, put on a thick coat and waited.

Person: Can you speak the news while I work? My hands are full of soil.
Assistant: Of course. Which news would you like: local, sports or world?
Person: Local, and not too much. Three headlines, fewer than yesterday.
Assistant: Here are three. The town is planning a new bridge. A school fair is on Saturday. A bakery is closing for repairs.
Person: Is there any news about the garden show in September?
Assistant: I can't find anything about it yet. I can look again tomorrow if you like.
Person: Yes please. I want my neat rows of tulips to be ready.

Imran sat in the dorm room with an empty stomach and a lecture at seven. The food Imran had ordered online was late. "I'm starving, and it has been an hour," Imran said to the phone. The assistant understood and checked the order. It said the driver was two streets away and would arrive in about five minutes. Then Imran saw that the flat number on the screen was wrong. "Can you fix that? It's flat twelve, not twenty-one." The assistant changed the address on the order and sent a short note to the driver. A few minutes later someone knocked on the door. The food was still hot, and Imran made it to the lecture on time.

Person: I can't stand these phones. My girl has homework and I need some help.
Assistant: I can help. What would you like me to do for her homework?
Person: Remind her to read. Every day.
Assistant: Sure. What time should I remind her?
Person: After school. In twenty minutes? No, I mean at four o'clock.
Assistant: Got it. A daily reminder at four o'clock to read. Is that right?
Person: Yes, thank you. That was easy.

Heating keeps a home warm. A thermostat is a small dial or screen that tells the heater what temperature you want. When people feel cold, they say, make it warmer, or turn it up two degrees. When the room is too hot, they say, lower it a little. A weak radiator may need more time to warm a big room, so some people start the heating an hour early. Many thermostats record the temperature all day, so you can see when the house was coldest. Cooking with an oven or a microwave can warm a kitchen a little, but only the heating warms the whole home.

Ayita ran a small chocolate shop on Palm Street, and the morning was slow. While waiting for the first customers, Ayita said to the speaker on the counter, "Read me the local headlines and tell me if the street market is open on Saturday." The speaker read three headlines. One was about a new bakery, one was about road work, and one was about a school choir. Then it said the street market would open on Saturday at eight. Ayita smiled. Friendly neighbours often come in to chat, and now there was plenty to talk about. When the first customer walked in, Ayita said, "Did you hear about the new bakery?"

Yuki was kneeling in the garden with muddy hands, drawing up a plan to design a new flower bed. The soil was dry and hard, and the tablet on the bench was too far to touch. "Make the text bigger and read my notes out loud," Yuki said. The tablet made the letters twice as large and read the notes in a slow voice: tulips by the fence, herbs near the door, water twice a week. Then Yuki remembered the time. "And remind me to take my pill at noon." The tablet said the reminder was set. Yuki kept digging and listening to the notes, and did not need to wipe a single finger.

Remy had just moved to the city and found a small pool on the roof of the building. It was full of fallen leaves, and the water looked cold. From the roof, the mountain in the distance was lovely, but Remy wanted a swim. "Tell me the water temperature and print the cleaning schedule," Remy said to the phone. The phone said the water was eighteen degrees and that the pool was cleaned every Thursday. A moment later the printer in the lobby began to print the schedule. Remy picked up the page, saw that the pump would run until noon, and decided to wait a day for a warmer swim.

name: log_sleep_night
does: Writes down how a night of sleep went, such as a broken night, so the user can see patterns over time.
inputs: the night, how many hours were slept, and any notes, like a late supper of corn or a night on a ship
people say:
- I slept badly last night, write it down
- log that I woke up three times
- note that I only got five hours
- remember that I had a bad night after the late dinner
- save how I slept, please

name: laundry_ready_alert
does: Tells the user when a washer or dryer cycle is finished and the clothes are ready, and keeps a file of past cycles.
inputs: which machine, and whether the clothes are muddy from planting tomatoes or just everyday wear
people say:
- tell me when the wash is done
- is my dryer finished yet?
- ping me when the clothes are ready
- let me know when the laundry stops spinning
- I'm going out, shout when the machine is done

Someone wants a recipe made bigger for more people.
double it
Scale it up
make it bigger
Can you write the amounts again for eight people instead of four?
I am cooking the red lentil soup for twelve guests, so please make the recipe feed three times as many.
I need enough sauce to dress the salad for ten, how much of each thing?
The recipe says four servings, but we are six. Can you change the numbers?

Someone wants milk put on the shopping list.
add milk to my list
put eggs on the list
need bread on the shoping list
We are out of milk, can you put it on the list?
The main thing I need this week is rice, so please add it to my grocery list.
My baking class is tonight and I need flour, so write it on the list.
Put sugar on my list, I want to mix a cake tomorrow.

A baby monitor lets parents hear or see a baby from another room. A small microphone near the cot picks up sounds, and a speaker or phone plays them. Some monitors have a silver light that shows how loud the room is. Babies grow fast, and the days seem to fly by, so parents like a plan: feeding times, nap times and bedtime. They set reminders, like feed the baby at three. When the plan changes, people say, move the nap to two o'clock, or make the monitor louder, or turn it down a little. Short, quiet words work best, so a sleeping baby is not woken up.

name: make_my_drink
does: Starts the coffee machine or kettle so a creamy cup of coffee or tea is ready when the user comes back from the mailbox or wakes up.
inputs: the drink, how strong, how sweet, and whether to fold in milk or cream
people say:
- make me a strong coffee
- I need a cup of tea, not too sweet
- can you start the coffee machine?
- a latte with extra milk, please
- I'm up, get my morning drink going

Thabo woke up to a faint dripping sound and a wet patch near the kitchen wall. Half asleep, Thabo spoke to the home assistant. "Good morning. Could you please check the water use in the house? I think there might be a leak, and I would hate for the bill to be huge this month." The assistant connected to the water meter and said that water was running even though nothing was on. It pointed to the pipe near the main tap. Thabo remembered the chicken thawing in the sink, but that was not the problem. The assistant offered to close the main valve and Thabo said yes. The dripping stopped. Then Thabo asked it to find a plumber for the afternoon.

Sports fans like to follow matches and scores. A score shows how many points each team has. People ask, what's the score? or tell me when the game starts. Players train to run a longer distance or get stronger, and many keep notes about their training. When a new season begins, teams play on set days, and fans ask for reminders. Sometimes the plan changes, so people say, hang on, move my reminder to eight, or tell me when my team is winning. A short, clear request works best: the team, the day and the time.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water and soap. Before you start, you choose a program, the water temperature and the size of the load. A small load needs less water than a big one. While it runs, the screen shows how much time is left, and people ask, how long is left on the wash? When it stops, they get the clothes out and put them in the dryer or hang them up. If a stain is left on a shirt, people say, wash it again, or use a hotter wash. Many also ask to get a message when the machine finishes.

name: send_invites
does: Sends an invitation for a party or a breakfast gathering to the guests on a list.
inputs: who to invite, the date and time, the place, and any note, like for guests who travel a long way or need to bring heavy chairs
people say:
- invite everyone from my list to Saturday's party
- send out the invitations for mum's sixtieth
- tell the guests it starts at six
- ask Tom and Ana to come to the barbecue
- let my friends know about the party on the tenth
- can you message the whole family about Sunday?

Eleanor grabbed a bag and ran for the door. A plane was leaving in two hours, and the electricity bill was due tomorrow. "Excuse me, could you please pay the electricity bill today? I will be away for a week and I do not want to pay a late fee." The assistant said the bill was sixty-two dollars and paid it from the usual account. It sent a receipt to the phone. Eleanor had also been getting constant reminder messages about the bill, so Eleanor asked the assistant to reset them for next month. The assistant did that and wished Eleanor a good trip.

Cyclists use a bike computer or a phone to track a ride. It shows the distance, the speed and how long the ride took. People use it to plan a route, find a quiet road, or compare today's ride with last week's. A great ride might be longer or faster, but it can also just be fun. Some people carry a bag with a few pounds of tools and food, and they ask for the weather before they start. To change things, people say, show me a flatter route, or make the ride shorter, or tell me when I have gone ten miles.

Oksana was a driver, and the day began with snow. Parked outside a cafe, Oksana opened the phone and asked the home printer a question. "Is there paper left? I need the forms printed before I get home, but only half of them." The printer said there were only a few sheets in the tray and the black ink was low. The assistant offered to print half of the forms, ten pages, and add paper to the shopping list. "Yes, please." By the time Oksana got home, the pages were waiting on the table, and dinner was warm in the oven.

name: label_moving_box
does: Writes a label for a moving box and holds a list of what is inside it.
inputs: the room the box belongs to, what is inside, like a lemon squeezer and two pans, and how soon it will be needed, so urgent boxes are not unpacked late
people say:
- label this box kitchen
- put on the list that box five has the plates
- remember what's in the blue box
- make a tag for the bedroom stuff
- I need to know which box has the kettle

Sofia finished the morning in the garden and came into a living room full of hard sun. "Close the living room blinds, please, but do not close the bedroom curtains. I don't want it dark upstairs." The assistant closed the blinds downstairs and left the bedroom ones open. Sofia said, "That sofa was expensive, and I don't want the sun to fade it. And don't forget to open them again at five." The assistant said it would open the living room blinds at five o'clock. A person walking past on the street waved at the garden, and Sofia waved back, glad the room was cool.

name: remember_birthday
does: Saves a person's birthday to the user's account and reminds the user a full week before, in time to buy a card or a gift.
inputs: the person's name, the date, and an optional note, like a gift they hinted at
people say:
- remember my mum's birthday is June 4th
- don't let me forget Sam's birthday
- save Aunt Rosa's birthday, she was born on 12 October
- tell me a week before Dad's birthday
- note that Lena loves tea and add her birthday on the 20th

Someone wants fewer notifications from a social media app.
fewer alerts please
Half as many notifications, please.
I'm tired of the buzzing, turn the alerts down.
I don't care about every like, just tell me about messages.
Can you send me one summary a day instead of all the alerts?
My phone keeps buzzing on the beach and I want less of it.
Could you please cut my notifications to the important ones only, since I get far too many?

Arithmetic is the plain work with numbers: putting them together, taking one away, making groups of equal size, and sharing. People use it when they pay, cook or plan. If a bill is big, they might ask the assistant, what is forty plus twenty-five? or take ten from sixty. For equal sharing, they say, split ninety between three. When a long sum gets confusing, they ask the assistant to restart with the first number. A teacher gives a lesson on each of these, but in everyday life people just use quick words such as plus, minus, times and shared by.

Person: turn on the sprinker for ten minutes
Assistant: Which one? There are two zones, the front and the back.
Person: front please, the flowers by the shop door
Assistant: Done. The front sprinkler is on for ten minutes.
Person: great, they looked so pretty last june and i want them to bloom again
Assistant: Would you like me to water them every morning?
Person: yes, but skip the rainy days. i forgot yesterday because i did not sleep well
Assistant: Understood. Every morning at seven, except when it rains.

Francesca had a dream of visiting Japan, and today the ticket page showed a price in dollars. Francesca was not good with phones, so Francesca spoke slowly to the assistant. "How many euros is fifty dollars?" Then Francesca stopped. "No, wait, I mean pounds, not euros." The assistant said that was fine and gave the answer for pounds: fifty dollars was about forty pounds today. Under a clean blue sky, Francesca sat on a bench in the park and smiled. "That is not so bad," said Francesca. The assistant offered to say the number again if the rate changed, and Francesca said yes.

Someone wants to be reminded to take a coat when leaving the house.
Remind me to take my coat
coat reminder at 7
Remind me about my coat and my keys when I leave.
Could you nudge me before I go out to grab my coat, and tell me the weather?
I often forget my coat, so tell me before I leave.
Ping me at eight about the coat and the umbrella.
Please ask me about my coat each morning, and restart the reminder if I snooze it.

The kitchen was loud, with constant noise from the pans. Pilar was a cook, and a call with the owner was about to start. With flour on both hands, Pilar spoke to the phone. "Join meeting." The assistant opened the call, but the screen asked for a password. "What is the password?" the assistant asked. Pilar said it was in an email. The assistant found the email, read out the number, and typed it in. Then the call began. Pilar put the phone on the shelf and tried to follow the plan while the onions cooked.

Dragan was in the garden, standing by the little wooden bridge over the pond, when the laptop on the bench froze. The wireless link had dropped and the screen was stuck. Muddy hands made typing hard. "Restart laptop," Dragan said. The assistant warned that the battery was at eight percent and asked if that was okay. "Yes, go on." The laptop restarted, the wireless came back, and the screen woke up. Dragan carried it inside to the charger and sat down with a cup of tea.

Remy, a retired teacher, was about to fly to see a grandchild. The bag was by the door, and a bottle of wine for the host sat on top. "Could you please turn on the cameras and the alarm? I will be away for a week, and I think I left the back window open." The assistant switched on the cameras and the alarm and said the back window sensor showed it was open. Remy hurried to shut it, then said, "Thank you. Please send me a message if the motion sensor sees anything." The assistant said it would. Remy locked the door and called a taxi.

Sigrid did not trust new gadgets, but walked up the hill behind the house and had an idea for a poem. The page in the pocket was loose and the pencil was gone. "I would like to say something and have you write it down, please, because I always forget my ideas by the time I get home." The assistant said it was ready. Sigrid said the first lines of the poem, slowly. The assistant saved them as a voice note and a text note called Hill poem. Sigrid smiled. "Can you read it back?" The assistant did, and the lines sounded just right.

Rain poured down on the bus stop and the wind was bitter. Pooja, a student with a heavy bag, wrote the address on a napkin and then spoke to the phone. "Book me a taxi to the library, but not a shared one. And I don't want to be picked up at the front gate, it is closed." The assistant asked where to pick up, and Pooja said the side door on Green Street. It booked a private taxi to that corner and said the car would arrive in six minutes. Pooja put the napkin in a pocket and waited under the roof.

Someone wants to know what a price is in their own money.
How much is that in dollars?
The sign says forty euros, is that a lot for me?
I wish I knew what this costs at home.
A lawn mower here is three hundred pounds, what is that in dollars?
The tag says twenty-five francs. Is that mild or expensive for me?
I wonder what the pound is worth today.
Could you tell me what this costs back home? I can't work it out.

Someone wants to send a text to one friend, not to the whole group.
Text Anna, not the group chat
Message only Tom, not everyone
Send this to Mia alone: I'll be late. Don't put it in the family chat.
Tell Sam I'm unpacking boxes, but don't tell the others.
Write to Jo that the magazine arrived, please don't post it in the group.
Text my brother, but keep it short, I'm comfortable with a few words.
Please message Lee privately, and make sure it doesn't go to the book club chat.

Haruto turned on the kitchen tap and the water came out brown. Haruto was not good with technology and had learned a lesson: ask the phone first. "Call plumber," said Haruto. The assistant said there were two plumbers nearby and asked, "Do you want the nearest one or the cheapest?" Haruto said the nearest. The assistant booked a visit for four o'clock and sent the time to the phone. "Shall I remind you an hour before?" Haruto said yes, closed the tap and waited.

Zara came home after a long night shift. The house was quiet, and Zara's stomach was empty. "What is in the fridge?" Zara asked the speaker. The speaker said there were three eggs, some cheese and half a loaf of bread. Zara could already feel a cheese sandwich coming. Then Zara said, "We're out of milk and butter. Put them on the list, because I'm going shopping on the twelfth of March." The speaker added both to the shopping list and said it would remind Zara on the morning of the twelfth. Zara ate the sandwich and went to sleep.

Hassan swept the crumbs off the desk with one hand and held a melon in the other. The melon was a gift for an aunt who was flying in that evening. "Is the flight from Cairo on time, and what gate is it at?" Hassan asked the phone. The assistant said the plane was ten minutes early and would land at gate twelve. Hassan thanked the assistant and left the office, walking past a tall glass wall where the afternoon sun was shining. The melon felt heavy, but Hassan was happy.

Person: Hi, I'm new in the city and this is my first day in the flat. Can you open the blinds and unlock the balcony door?
Assistant: I can open the blinds. I can't unlock doors, because the lock is not connected to me. Sorry about that.
Person: That's fine. Which blinds can you open?
Assistant: There are blinds in the living room and the bedroom. Which would you like?
Person: The living room first. The sum I pay for this flat is big, so I want the sun.
Assistant: The living room blinds are open now.
Person: Thanks! Open the bedroom ones later, at eight.

When you order something from a shop or online, you pick the thing, the size and how you want to get it. A lovely jacket may come in small, medium or large, and people change the size if it does not fit. Delivery can be to your home or to a shop, and some places bring things late in the evening, when the moon is already out. A cool bag keeps food cold on the way. People say, send it to my office, or I want to return this, or make it a size bigger. Most shops let you send things back within a few weeks.

A printer puts words and pictures from a computer or phone onto paper. A scanner does the opposite: it makes a picture of a paper page, like a letter or a pencil drawing, and saves it on the computer. When the printer runs low on ink, it tells you which color is gone, for example yellow. People say, print two copies, or print only page three, or scan this and send it to me. After a scan, you can scroll through the pages on the screen and check that every one looks clear. If the paper tray is empty, people ask for more paper to be added to the shopping list.
